normalization: Physical period two, exp(i*pi*k*x), original coefficient q(mode(-k)), normalized original dual action with factor1/2. The upper source coupling is at q(mode(-2*n)) and the lower coupling is at q(mode(2*n)); the factor2 is retained.
proof_details: Full original H-minus-one/H1 duality and commutativity of actual H1 multiplication give the singular Green identity for every complex H-minus-one potential. No endpoint sum interchange is postulated.

Every reconstructed H1 amplitude satisfies the actual physical spectral pencil with exactly its finite two-mode residual. The inherited off-diagonal bilinear symmetry forces equality of the two actual diagonal corrections.
The original two-sided endpoint tail inverse and both opposite shifted norms yield the uniform coefficient error 2*C_r*n^(r-1/2)*norm(q)^2, with every source spectral weight retained.
The genuine complementary Fourier resolvent identity controls spectral variation globally on the corrected closed strip, using absolutely convergent original rows and both shifted inverse bounds.
The existing cutoff makes the actual diagonal a Lipschitz contraction with constant1/8. No Cauchy estimate based on the printed12n strip is needed.

The actual determinant factors as (lambda-pi^2*n^2-a_n)^2-b_n*b_-n. Its full-strip coupling supremum is proved finite. Each root shift is bounded by that actual supremum; diagonal contraction and the triangle inequality yield the literal source sqrt6 root-separation constant.

sourceLemma2_11_uniform combines the existing two-zero analytic-order counts on the source4sqrt(n) disc and entire strip, the stronger sqrt(n)/4 localization, and the full source root-separation estimate. The cutoff precedes every original complex potential in the norm ball.
qualifications: Multiplicity in the zero count is analytic order of the actual effective determinant. Equality with algebraic multiplicity of the physical singular Hill operator remains open.

The scalar original-distribution Lemma2.9 wrapper is explicitly the unit spectral weight scale. The arbitrary-weight coefficient error is proved separately; the sharper source weighted diagonal bound involving the unweighted potential norm is not claimed here.
